how_the_pin_works.principle: DERIVED, never transcribed. Nothing in the test file hardcodes an expected return set. _status_contract_from_source reads each implementation's execute() with `ast` and reports the status literals it can actually return, so the pin goes red from EITHER side -- implementation drift or schema drift.
how_the_pin_works.why_ast_not_a_call: Calling execute() needs a live `hou`. Driving it with a MagicMock `hou` is banned by Law 1 for host-behaviour assertions. The status literal in the source IS the fact under test, so reading the literal is the honest measurement -- the same idiom, for the same reason, as test_solaris_tool_registration._registered_commands.
how_the_pin_works.refuses_rather_than_guesses: Any return shape the reader cannot reduce to string literals RAISES (UnreadableStatus) instead of returning a smaller set. A reader that silently skips what it cannot parse measures less and less over time while still reporting green -- that is the D1 '218/218 by construction' defect, and it is the failure mode this file exists to avoid.
how_the_pin_works.anti_vacuity: test_schema_declares_a_nonempty_status_enum and test_implementation_emits_a_nonempty_status_set exist because `set() == set()` would otherwise pass while pinning nothing.
how_the_pin_works.calibration_controls: 11 of the 34 tests check the INSTRUMENT before it is trusted: 2 positive controls (a known status set; the nested ternary) and 9 negative controls (computed status, bare name, ** unpacking, missing status key, bare return, non-dict return, no returns, no execute, non-literal key). This is the paired negative control probe_phase3_layout was faulted for lacking.

the_drift_reconciled.clean_on_arrival: component_builder, scene_template, import_megascans -- all three declared exactly {created, already_exists} and returned exactly that. Their pins passed on the first run, before any edit.

findings.summary: The drift was TWO schemas, not one. R33 and the brief both name only set_purpose. create_variants declared a third status `extended` that execute() has never returned. Same defect class, same blast radius: the model was told to expect an outcome that cannot occur.
findings.disposition: Fixed in this leg -- `extended` removed. The pin now prevents its return.

findings.summary: `extended` may have been describing a REAL behavioural gap rather than being invented. The idempotency guard is all-or-nothing: `if all(f'mat_{vn}' in existing_names or f'geo_{vn}' in existing_names for vn in variant_names)`. A PARTIAL overlap therefore falls through, builds only the missing variants, and reports `created` -- indistinguishable from a call that built everything from scratch. Under Law 3 ('status describes what happened') that is arguably imprecise.
findings.disposition: NOT fixed here. Changing it is an implementation change and the brief's scope fence (line 23) routes implementation questions to H2 re-qualification. The reasoning is recorded as a comment at the edit site so the next reader meets it. Escalated as H1-R1.

findings.summary: TOOL_RETURN['properties'] is under-declared in four of five tools. Keys execute() returns but no schema declares: `strategy` (component_builder), `primitive_paths` (scene_template), `message`/`reason`/`configure_node`/`prim_path`/`usd_purpose` (set_purpose). ZERO tools declare a property they never return -- the false direction is clean.
findings.disposition: Pinned in ONE direction only, deliberately. JSON Schema `properties` is an open map here (no additionalProperties:false), so an emitted-but-undeclared key leaves the schema TRUE and merely under-documented, whereas a declared-but-never-emitted key makes it FALSE. Only the false direction is a correctness surface; the other is a judgement about how much to advertise. Escalated as H1-R2.

findings.summary: The `purpose` property's description read 'The purpose that was assigned.' That is false on the `noop` path, where execute() echoes the REQUESTED purpose while authoring nothing. Same misinformation class as the enum drift, one level down.
findings.disposition: Fixed -- the description now says it is the requested purpose and points the caller at `status`. Not pinned by a test (prose is not mechanically checkable against behaviour); recorded so it is not mistaken for an unforced edit.

findings.summary: Brief item 2's exclusion of tool_audit is independently corroborated: the module exports TOOL_AUDIT / TOOLS_NEW=5 / TOOLS_EXTENDED=2 / TOOLS_COVERED=2 and has no TOOL_NAME, no TOOL_SCHEMA, no TOOL_RETURN; no tool_audit.py implementation exists. Its own TOOLS_NEW=5 names exactly the five tools that were pinned.
findings.disposition: Written as a TEST rather than a comment (test_tool_audit_is_a_design_document_not_a_tool) so the exclusion expires on its own the day someone gives tool_audit an implementation. Mutation M13 proves it fires.

findings.summary: A SECOND writer was executing this identical brief in the identical worktree concurrently. Observed live: tests/test_solaris_tool_registration.py rewritten 209 -> 480+ lines at 14:50:23; tests/test_solaris_schema_return_contract.py created at 14:51:28 and still growing at 14:52:53; all five schema_*.py edited at 14:51:42. My own first baseline suite run died with PermissionError on pytest-current, contending with the other process. This is Constitution Article V's named failure ('two agents in one directory produce interleaved commits, a corrupted suite baseline, and findings that cannot be attributed').
findings.disposition: STOPPED before writing anything, escalated to the human, and re-ran the leg in a fresh isolated worktree (.claude/worktrees/h1-schemas-b, branch repair/h1-schemas-b, based on commit 70ed8ef so none of the other writer's uncommitted edits were inherited). The original worktree was reverted to clean at 14:57:44 by the human. Escalated as H1-R3.
findings.independent_corroboration: The two runs reached the same two conclusions independently -- set_purpose 3-declared-vs-5-real, and create_variants `extended` unreachable. Two readers agreeing from different starts is evidence for the finding, which is the one useful by-product of the collision.

findings.summary: The mutation harness restored files with pathlib.write_text(), which on Windows re-encodes LF -> CRLF. Seven implementation files that this leg never intended to touch came back byte-different, showing as modified with git warning 'CRLF will be replaced by LF'. Content was identical; only line endings moved. Same species as R24 (a tool wrote bytes nobody read back).
findings.disposition: Caught by checking `git status` after the battery rather than trusting the harness's own restore. The seven were restored with `git checkout --`, and schema_set_purpose.py (a real edit that had also been CRLF-damaged by mutation M7's restore) was renormalised to LF. Final tree is exactly 3 files, LF-clean, zero git line-ending warnings. A byte-mode restore (read_bytes/write_bytes) is the correct pattern for any future mutation harness.

for_ruling.question: create_variants: should `extended` come BACK as a real implementation behaviour, or is collapsing the partial-overlap case into `created` correct?
for_ruling.context: Removing it from the schema was forced -- brief item 5 says fix schemas to match reality, and the tool demonstrably never returns it. But that made a real ambiguity invisible: after this leg, nothing distinguishes 'built all four variants' from 'built one, the other three already existed'. Restoring a distinct status is a Law 3 improvement; leaving it is defensible if callers do not care which. Either way the pin will force the schema to follow.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article I -- a value judgement between defensible options. Implementation change, so it belongs to H2 re-qualification (brief line 23), not to H1.
for_ruling.recommendation: Fold into H2's re-qualification of the Solaris family rather than opening a separate leg. The marginal cost there is near zero since H2 is already reading these implementations.

for_ruling.question: Should the return-property contract be pinned in BOTH directions -- i.e. must every key execute() returns also be declared in TOOL_RETURN?
for_ruling.context: I pinned only the false direction (a declared property must be emittable) and documented the asymmetry in the test module. The rationale: JSON Schema properties is an open map here, so undeclared extras leave the schema true. The counter-argument is that R33's own logic applies -- the model reasons on what it is told, and seven real return keys it is never told about (H1-F3) are seven affordances it cannot use. Pinning both directions would go red today on four of five tools.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Article I -- how strict the advertised contract should be is a product judgement, not something provable from the tree. Deliberately left as a finding rather than silently widened.
for_ruling.recommendation: Pin it, but as its own small leg with the schema fills authored deliberately -- not as an unplanned expansion of H1.

for_ruling.question: Two agents were dispatched onto the same H1 worktree simultaneously. What in the dispatch path allowed that, and should the orchestrator hold a lock?
for_ruling.context: H1-F6. Article V mandates a worktree per parallel agent, but nothing enforced it -- the constraint is prose, not a gate. The collision was caught only because I checked `git status` against a file I had already read. A leg that did not happen to re-read a file it had cached would have committed a merge of two agents' work and attributed it to one.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Process/gate design -- Article IV says enforcement belongs in the definition, not the instruction. A .lock file in the worktree, or an orchestrator-side registry, is the obvious shape, but which one is a design call.
for_ruling.recommendation: Cheapest real fix: the dispatcher writes .claude/worktrees/<leg>/.dispatch-lock naming the leg, model and start time, and refuses to dispatch into a worktree that already has one -- the same shape as commit 70ed8ef's 'refuse to dispatch into a missing brief'.

for_ruling.question: This leg's branch is repair/h1-schemas-b, not the leg-named repair/h1-schemas. Merge accordingly, or rebase onto the canonical name first?
for_ruling.context: The fresh worktree needed its own branch (git will not check out one branch in two worktrees) and repair/h1-schemas was still occupied by the other writer at the time. The work is three files off 70ed8ef with no conflicts; repair/h1-schemas is now clean at that same commit, so a fast-forward or cherry-pick is trivial.
for_ruling.why_escalated: Gate C -- merge is never automated. Flagging the naming mismatch so it is not discovered at merge time.
for_ruling.recommendation: Cherry-pick the single commit onto repair/h1-schemas and delete repair/h1-schemas-b, so the leg name matches the branch the orchestrator expects.
